title: Alphabet Snaps Its Longest Monthly Losing Streak as AI Momentum Returns
summary: Alphabet opened September by ending its longest monthly losing streak in over a decade, with Google Cloud up 82% year over year and heavy AI capex now in focus.
body_markdown:
The endorsement extends beyond the operating results. Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway now counts Alphabet among its largest equity positions, a notable signal from an investor who has historically been cautious on expensive technology names.


## The other side of the trade: capex


None of this comes cheap, and a balanced view has to weigh the cost. Alphabet has raised its 2026 capital-expenditure outlook toward roughly 205 billion dollars, up from a midpoint near 185 billion, and management has signaled that spending will likely climb again in 2027.


The company recently reported negative free cash flow for the first time since going public, a direct consequence of building AI infrastructure at scale. Bulls see that spend as the price of defending and extending a cloud franchise growing 82 percent a year. Skeptics see a bill whose payback is not yet proven. Both can be right for a while, which is exactly why the stock has been volatile.


## What to Watch From This News


- Cloud growth durability: whether the 82 percent pace holds, or decelerates, in the next earnings report.
- Free cash flow: how quickly heavy AI capex starts converting into cash generation rather than draining it.
- The competitive read-across to Microsoft and Amazon, whose own cloud growth rates set the bar for Alphabet.
- New model releases, which have become a near-term driver of the stock in their own right.


## Bottom line


Alphabet's September rebound is a reminder that in the current market, AI credibility is earned through shipping, not spending alone. The cloud franchise gives the bull case something real to point to, and the capex surge gives the bear case something equally real to worry about.


For long-term investors, the more useful frame is not whether the stock rebounded this week, but whether the returns on all that AI investment eventually justify the outlay. Nothing here is a guarantee in either direction, and the volatility of the past few months is a fair warning that the market has not made up its mind.
